Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cdrgam.cli 0.5.0

  • Resolved identities no longer depend on the R version. They hashed a serialization header that records the writing R version, so upgrading R made every artifact stale. Identities change once with this release, so artifacts made by earlier releases are stale and are rebuilt by cdrgam run.

  • SVG visualizations need a working Cairo SVG device; without one, such as on macOS without XQuartz, a run that requests svg output fails with that reason instead of publishing an artifact without the file.

  • New cdrgam methods command. It writes a cited methods section for the selected work items in RTF (the default), Markdown, or LaTeX, together with supplementary tables and a methods.json trace. Several projects can be described in one report. See docs/methods-reports.md. Requires cdrgam 0.5.0 or later for methods_facts().

  • New test definitions, under definitions/tests/. terms requests the whole-function tests that summary() reports for native model terms, mgcv smooths and IRF terms alike, selected by label: terms: ['s(time)']. Parametric terms are included and get mgcv’s per-term Wald tests. cdrgam def terms [-m MODEL ...] prints each fitted model’s labels; fits now also record parametric-terms.csv. cdrgam run -t MODEL, when no test has that name, creates a test of every term of the model and runs it. effects and estimands estimate and test derived summary statistics of fitted effects: weighted contrasts, means, areas, peak lags and values, and Wood’s whole-functional tests of compositions. Effects use the visualization value language and are evaluated on one joint coefficient distribution. cdrgam run -t NAME writes results/tests/NAME/tests.tsv, tab-separated for column -t -s $'\t'. --test/-t selects tests in def, plan, run, stop, log, and purge. Estimands need a cdrgam release with effect_inference().

  • Simultaneous bands read the effect covariance from one core evaluation, instead of one evaluation per point. A line of spr-main with 40 band points takes about 3 seconds instead of 70. Their critical values, and those of bands at peaks, now come from cdrgam’s simultaneous_critical_value(), so the CLI no longer computes them itself. Simultaneous intervals need a cdrgam release with that function and report an error asking to update cdrgam otherwise.

  • cdrgam def edit accepts * globs and re: regular expressions, as def ls, def val, and def rm do, and opens each existing match in turn: cdrgam def edit -P rep -v '*-wlen'. Literal names still create missing definitions; patterns cannot be combined with --source.

  • Line and point plots draw a thin line at zero effect in each panel whose vertical range includes zero. render.zero_line: false, or clearing Line at zero in cdrgam viz, turns it off. Existing visualizations keep their identities and draw the line when they next render.

  • render.panel_width and render.panel_height fix the size of the plot panel in inches, and the rendered file grows to fit the axes, titles, and legend. Figures with different legends then have identical panels. They cannot be combined with width or height. cdrgam.cli now requires ggplot2 4.0.0 or later.

  • Each line in the cdrgam viz line list has Duplicate, which adds a copy below it labeled “(copy)”. The line being edited is marked with a tinted background and a bar on its left instead of a blue fill, so its links stay readable.

  • render.ylim: [low, high] sets the vertical display range of line, point, and bar plots without dropping rows; either end may be null. In cdrgam viz, Vertical axis range sets it, and X range under Options sets where lines are evaluated, as numbers or expressions such as mean - 2 * sd.

  • cdrgam purge selectors also match names that no longer have a definition, such as a visualization removed with cdrgam def rm. Their results, work directories, logs, and registry records can be purged by name, as cdrgam status already lists them.

  • render.reverse_palette, Reverse palette order in cdrgam viz, starts the palette from its last color, so with okabe-ito the first line is black and the second grey. Spread palettes such as viridis are reversed end to end. The viewer’s line list shows the same colors.

  • In cdrgam viz, X tick values typed for lines now set the plot’s ticks. They had reached the exported render YAML but not the plot itself.

  • render.tick_labels sets the text of the x tick labels: one per break in the order written, or one per distinct x value when there are no breaks. In cdrgam viz, X tick labels sets it for typed X tick values.

  • render.geometry: connected-point, Connected points in cdrgam viz, draws points with their error bars and joins each series’ points in x order with a thin line, without an interval band, to show trends.

  • lag: peak-pointwise(LABEL) and peak-pointwise-neg(LABEL) hold each point at the peak lag of another term, found at that point’s values of the named term’s predictors. For example, an interaction can be read at the lag where one of its main effects peaks. The named term’s predictors must be predictors of the plotted term. Simultaneous bands draw both terms from the same coefficient sample, so they include the uncertainty in the borrowed peak lags.

  • The cdrgam run progress line shows a braille spinner in place of the color-cycling dot. It uses nro’s frames and its 0.08-second frame interval.

  • render.breaks labels chosen x values on a continuous axis without changing where the effect is evaluated. In cdrgam viz, X tick values now sets it for lines, which stay on the evaluation grid instead of being evaluated only at the ticks. Points and bars are still evaluated at the tick values, and Grid points per axis is hidden while it has no effect. An empty grid-points field uses the default of 200.

  • Effect grids are no longer separate work items or cached. A visualization evaluates its effects from the fit each time it renders, so its figure always reflects the installed cdrgam. The plotted numbers are written beside the figure in results/visualizations/NAME/: effect-grid.csv and its companions, or line-ID-grid.csv and its companions for each line. Effect directories under .cdrgam/work/ from earlier versions are no longer read and can be deleted.

  • Rendered visualizations are written to results/visualizations/NAME/ instead of results/models/MODEL/visualizations/NAME/, because a visualization with lines may draw from several models. Existing visualizations re-render into the new location on the next run. The legend of a lines plot no longer shows a line title.

  • Parallel jobs that share a work item, such as a fit used by several visualizations, no longer conflict. Claiming and publishing an item hold a per-item lock, and a new attempt is marked running at once, so another job no longer deletes it as stale. A job that reaches an item another job is running waits, then reuses the published artifact. Under the scheduler, the worker takes other ready work instead. Creating a shared results directory no longer fails when another job creates it first.

  • cdrgam purge --work --logs with a workload selector removes only the selected work items’ attempts, archived artifacts, and logs. It previously removed the project’s entire work and log directories, including files that belonged to other models. Without a workload selector, both options still remove the whole directories.

  • Visualizations accept geometry: point, which draws estimates as points with error bars, and geometry: bar, which draws them as bars with error bars. interval: errorbar is their default. Series at one x position are placed side by side.

  • render.spacing draws a numeric x-axis at its evaluated values, one tick per value, spaced uniformly in sorted order or linearly by value.

  • render.statistic: peak-lag plots the peak lags a query used, with their posterior intervals, as points or bars.

  • render.palette accepts grey, the viridis options, and ColorBrewer palette names in addition to default and rainbow. The peak timeline uses the same colors as the main plot.

  • render.palette: okabe-ito gives the viewer’s eight line colors: the colorblind-safe Okabe-Ito colors except yellow, then grey and black.

  • The viewer draws its plots from the same plot specification as rendered visualizations. Lines keep their colors; with more than eight lines the viewer switches every line to viridis and says so under the plot. Heatmaps use the rendered surfaces’ diverging colors, symmetric about zero.

  • The viewer’s Appearance panel offers the render settings that apply to it: points and bars, peak lags, intervals, tick spacing, palettes including custom gradients, the peak timeline, titles, and theme. It replaces the Show intervals option and the surface Display buttons; surfaces add contour-only and heatmap-with-contours displays and a standard-error heatmap. A test fails when a render field has no viewer control and no stated reason.

  • Show render YAML in the viewer prints its appearance settings as a render block for a visualization definition.

  • Simultaneous intervals for values that use a peak, such as lag: peak or peak-pointwise, now include the uncertainty about where the peak lies: posterior draws each re-find the peak before the band is formed. Lines at peak-pointwise accept simultaneous intervals. This needs cdrgam’s new sample_effect_coefficients(), and changes the bands of the irf-predictor preset, which plots at peak lags.

  • Visualization definitions accept lines: one effect per line, each with its own term, model, axes, reference, composition, and grouping, drawn on one plot. The definition’s query gives defaults that lines inherit and may override. The viewer evaluates every line through the same code as cdrgam run, draws the same figure, and exports its lines, options, and appearance as such a definition under Definition YAML.

  • render.theme accepts every native ggplot2 theme (grey, gray, bw, linedraw, light, dark, minimal, classic, void, test), and render.y_zero: true keeps zero on the vertical axis. The viewer offers both under Appearance and starts in classic; definitions still default to paper.

  • The viewer keeps its form, including the model, term, axes, fixed and reference values, and the Options panel, across Refresh data, page reloads, and server restarts, as it already kept lines and appearance.

  • In the viewer, the peak timeline appears whenever a line uses a peak, unless Show peak lags under the plot is off, and its rows carry the legend labels. Its ticks stay within their own row, and stacked panels leave room for each x-axis title.

  • Points at one x position sit in adjacent columns one point wide, so clusters at different positions stay apart; bars still fill 80% of the gap. Arrows in the lines list reorder lines, the palette menu shows each palette’s colors, and X tick values under Options evaluates lines at chosen x values with a tick at each.

  • lag: peak-pointwise and peak-pointwise-neg hold each evaluation point at its own peak lag: the lag where the query’s effect, after its reference subtraction, is largest or smallest at that point. Effect artifacts record the lags in effect-pointwise-peaks.csv with posterior intervals, and line and point plots, rendered and in the viewer, add a panel of peak lag over the x-axis. This needs estimate_effect(points=) from the development cdrgam.

  • Under composition: total, and the viewer’s Total composition, peak and peak-neg locate the peak of the total response to a one-SD increase rather than of the term alone. An interaction’s peak now matches the curve its lines show. Peak tables gain a composition column.

  • The viewer’s reference fields cover only the fixed axes, lag included; a plotted axis keeps its value in the reference. Previously each plotted predictor was set to its model default, which dropped the term from the reference. While a line is being edited, Update line and Cancel replace Add line.

  • The peak timeline keeps its lane order when only some peaks have posterior draws; a lane without draws was drawn at the top.

  • The vertical axis of a rendered surface is titled by its mapped column, or ylab, instead of “Effect on linear predictor”.

  • Invalid render choices name the field and its accepted values, as in render.theme must be one of paper, minimal, slides.

  • render.palette also accepts a list of two or more colors (hex, rgb(R, G, B), or R color names). The plot colors its lines, points, or bars at equal steps from the first color to the last.

cdrgam.cli 0.4.0

  • Lag values accept peak(<term>) and peak-neg(<term>), which hold every term at the lag where the named term’s response is largest or smallest. <term> is a term label from the effect catalog, such as peak(irf(1)).

  • Effects that use a peak write effect-peaks.csv with each peak lag and a level interval from posterior draws of that lag, and the draws in effect-peak-draws.csv. uncertainty.peak_draws sets the number of draws (default 1000; 0 skips them). The draws need cdrgam 0.4.0.

  • Line plots that use a peak can show a timeline of peak lags, intervals, and draws below the main panel. render.peaks is auto (when terms were held at different peak lags), always, or never. The viewer draws the same timeline.

  • cdrgam viz on a root without Slurm, or with --local, prints the viewer’s address and opens the browser; --no-browser suppresses that. A local viewer makes no Slurm calls, so it can run where Slurm does not, such as Windows. --stop and --restart now explain that a local viewer is stopped by interrupting it.

  • Linux hosted checks run on Ubuntu 24.04.

cdrgam.cli 0.3.0

  • Visualization definitions accept preset: irf-lag and preset: irf-predictor. irf-lag plots every ungrouped IRF with one predictor over lag, at the predictor’s mean plus one SD relative to its mean, and can add irf(1). irf-predictor plots the same terms over their predictor values at a fixed lag, 0 by default. Both use simultaneous 95% intervals and a rainbow palette by default, and hold time axes at their training means.

  • Effect-query axis values and references accept arithmetic over an axis’s training mean, sd, and median, such as mean + 2 * sd, and a range: [low, high] grid. Lag values also accept peak (or peak-pos) and peak-neg, the lag at which a term’s response is largest or smallest. A wildcard reference "*" applies to every predictor of each term, and the term selector field interacting keeps or drops terms with more than one predictor.

  • uncertainty: {kind: simultaneous} replaces pointwise limits with simultaneous ones over each term’s grid, computed in the harness from estimate_effect() alone. The viewer offers the same intervals, accepts value expressions in its fixed and reference fields, and now starts unvaried axes at lag 0 and training means rather than medians.

  • Effect queries now hold unspecified time and predictor axes at their training means rather than medians. Grids from existing definitions that relied on the median change.

  • Effects are now evaluated one term at a time. Effect grids gain predictor and predictor_value columns for terms with one predictor, and critical_value for simultaneous intervals. Line renderings accept palette: rainbow and facet scales.

  • Published fit diagnostics include newton_step_max and predicted_decrease_floor from the core, beside predicted_decrease and the raw gradient maxima. A gradient above the tolerance along a well-curved direction can then be read against the negligible Newton step it implies.

  • Rerunning work after its Slurm worker ran out of memory no longer fails at once. The killed worker left its attempt marked running, and when the node reused its process ID for a process the scheduler could not inspect, the attempt was treated as still active, so every new claim failed. An attempt whose Slurm job has ended is now inactive, as is one whose process belongs to another user. When the scheduler fails work without an active attempt, it records the reason on the latest attempt, so status no longer shows the earlier attempt’s error. When squeue no longer knows the job, as happens once Slurm purges a finished job, Slurm accounting decides instead of the recorded process ID.

  • Definitions without fit.rescale_predictors now fit with rescaled predictors, because the core default changed to true. Their model identities and fitted results change accordingly; set fit.rescale_predictors: false to keep native-unit fits.

  • diagnostics.yml now includes the core’s notes, the interior and full outer-Hessian minimum eigenvalues, and one hessian_boundary record per smoothing parameter on the boundary of its range, with its profile bound. These require the development cdrgam that classifies boundary smoothing parameters.

  • Effect visualization queries accept reference, which subtracts the effect at reference axis values, with default leaving a predictor at the model default, and test: true, which writes joint Wald tests to effect-tests.csv. Both require the development cdrgam that provides test_effect(). With composition: total, interaction terms such as irf(wlen, repetition_index, k_p=list(NULL, 3)) now include their lower-order terms, which follows the core change.

  • The deviation composition is removed from visualization queries, layers, and the viewer. It returned the same values as term. Use grouping: deviation for grouped deviations.

  • cdrgam viz has a Reference control. Each line or surface can subtract the effect at reference values of its predictors; an empty field uses the model default. The line label records the reference, and saved lines keep it across reloads.

  • The viewer’s lines pane has a fixed height and scrolls, so the plot keeps its size as lines are added. The pane could previously be pushed out of view.

  • Line renderings draw a separate curve for each value of every varying axis other than x. Several values of a moderator were previously joined into one path. Numeric color and linetype mappings with at most 12 values use a discrete legend.

  • cdrgam purge builds its selection in seconds for projects with many models and datasets. It previously built and renormalized a path for every model and dataset combination against every target, which took more than 25 minutes for a project with 92 models and 65 datasets; it now builds paths only for work directories that exist.

  • Model definitions accept fit.center_predictors (true or false), passed to the core package’s linear-predictor centering.

  • Adds cdrgam viz, a browser viewer for completed fits. It plots effect lines, including several lines from different fits on one plot, and two-axis surfaces, with fixed values for the remaining tensor axes. On Slurm roots the server runs in a per-user Slurm job that later calls reuse. Its Refresh data button picks up new and refitted results, and its Restart server button reloads installed code without a new Slurm job. The viewer’s dependencies (shiny, bslib, plotly, jsonlite, later) are optional.

  • Publishes each finished autosimplification fit to the model’s results directory as it completes. Earlier fits move to model_history/. When no allowed simplification resolves the remaining fit warnings, the last fit stays published with its warnings, status reports an error, and dependent work does not run.

  • Keeps workers connected when the scheduler restarts on the same node. Process start times were stored with about 8 significant digits, so a live scheduler or attempt could look dead and workers ignored the scheduler’s new address. A worker that cannot report a nonconverged or unresolved fit now stops cleanly instead of failing.

cdrgam.cli 0.2.1

  • Repairs release-tag validation for annotated tag messages containing Git’s formatting syntax.

cdrgam.cli 0.2.0

  • Gives clean installations a writable, cross-platform default CDR-GAM root in R’s user data directory. Root-local .cdrgam/site.yml, registry, scheduler state, and projects form one movable harness instance. CDRGAM_ROOT switches that complete instance without splitting configuration from data.
  • Replaces the exported checkout argument with cdrgam_root. Existing sites migrate by placing their scheduler fields and concurrency setting in <CDRGAM_ROOT>/.cdrgam/site.yml and omitting the now-implicit cdrgam_root field.
  • Speeds up work-graph construction by reusing source checksums while file size and modification time are unchanged and by removing redundant filesystem probes from managed-path construction.
  • Reports the current cdrgam run stage on standard error. Interactive terminals receive an in-place, color-rotating activity indicator.
  • Makes purge remove matching artifacts, attempts, logs, and registry records, and strengthens internal module boundaries for focused development tests.

cdrgam.cli 0.1.0

  • Establishes the first public development release of the CDR-GAM project harness.
  • Provides version-controlled project definitions, validation, dependency planning, local execution, and shared Slurm orchestration.
  • Manages atomic artifacts, logs, status, cleanup, publication, and retrieval across projects in one configured harness instance.
